summary: I checked the Fubini theorem and its proof (the Darboux-sum sandwich L(f,P) ≤ L(φ̲,P_A) ≤ U(φ̲,P_A) ≤ U(φ̄,P_A) ≤ U(f,P) and the companion chain with L(φ̄,P_A)), the corollary for continuous functions, all three counterexamples (the dense dyadic set χ_S example, the x=1/2 Dirichlet-section example, and the unbounded antisymmetric (x²−y²)/(x²+y²)² example with the values π/4 and −π/4), the vertical-section (normal domain) theorem with its boundary/measure-zero and zero-extension arguments, both worked examples (disc area π and the order swap giving (e−1)/2), the supplement's remarks on Fubini–Tonelli and the informal analogies, and both problems/solutions (the tetrahedron volume 1/6 and the parameter integral). Every cited result is used consistently with its quoted statement (Lebesgue's criterion, measure-zero properties .3 and .4, Jordan-measurability criterion .1/.3, Jordan additivity .1, box-integral properties .3, box-refinement, and the Riemann criterion). I found no false statement, no non-routine gap, and no circularity.
